title: Morris Brown boarding school band and learning to read
summary: At Morris Brown he plays in the band without reading, learning by watching the other trombonists' slide positions.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: How long was it before you started working, I mean, even as a youngster, say at 14, how long was it before you started playing say around Atlanta and in that area?
Well, I did, say, my brother was teaching and he put me in that boarding school in Atlanta and I played there. I played in the band in college.
What was the name of the boarding school?
Yeah, that's a famous school now.
Yeah, and I played and still couldn't read a note.
Well, when did you start learning to read?

He had me learning ... and the first tune was 'Poet and Peasant' ... every trombone player. So I'm looking at the music and he got up, stand up and walk around and he went on in this ear and planted the note and I'm watching the positions on the trombones.
You're watching the other trombone players?
Always eyes goin', that's why they so messed up now. other guy's positions are. So,
